rationale: Manually patching `timetable_type` across hundreds of tests is tedious and error-prone; a constructor default removes the need entirely.

rule: In `GitDagBundle._initialize()`, always assign and properly close `self.repo` before returning early from a cached-version path when `prune_dotgit_folder=False`.
trigger: diff introduces an early `return` inside `_initialize()` of a git bundle after `_local_repo_has_version()` without assigning `self.repo`
rationale: `get_current_version()` falls back to the raw `self.version` string (e.g. a tag) instead of the resolved HEAD SHA when `self.repo` is not set, producing an observable behaviour change versus a first-time initialise.

evidence.excerpt: with this early-return path `get_current_version()` will return the raw `self.version` string

rule: Treat `self.version` in `GitDagBundle` as a commit-ish (tag, short SHA, branch); always resolve it via `repo.commit(self.version).hexsha` before comparing to `repo.head.commit.hexsha`.
trigger: diff compares `self.version` directly to `repo.head.commit.hexsha` (string equality) inside a git bundle method
rationale: `self.version` is used elsewhere as a general commit-ish; direct string comparison against a full 40-char hexsha silently breaks the optimisation for tags and short SHAs.

evidence.excerpt: `self.version` is treated elsewhere as a general "commit-ish"

rule: Only include an entry in a provider's `changelog.rst` when that provider's own source files are changed; omit entries for changes that only touch tests in another provider.
trigger: diff adds a bullet in `providers/<name>/docs/changelog.rst` for a PR whose diff is limited to test files of a different provider
rationale: Changelog entries are user-facing; a test-only change in a sibling provider has no user-visible impact on the listed provider.

evidence.excerpt: changes only the tests so nothing to notify users about

rule: Place forward-looking compatibility notes (e.g. new Python version support caveats) in a provider changelog above the upcoming release section, not inside or below an already-published release block.
trigger: diff inserts a `.. note::` or compatibility banner inside or after an existing versioned release block in `changelog.rst`
rationale: A note about the next release must appear above that release's section so it is visible to users upgrading to that version.

evidence.excerpt: this banner now must be moved above the 21.0.0 as it will be relevant with next release

rule: Add new Google provider documentation as `.rst` files integrated into the existing docs structure, not as standalone `.md` files.
trigger: diff adds a new `.md` file under `providers/google/docs/`
rationale: Google provider docs follow the RST format with links to examples; adding a separate Markdown file breaks the consistent documentation structure.

evidence.excerpt: This shouldn't be added as a separate file, please add all information to rst document

rule: Bump a provider cross-dependency lower-bound version constraint only when the API change is genuinely breaking; additive changes with a default-`None` parameter do not require a version bump.
trigger: diff raises a `>=` version floor on `apache-airflow-providers-*` in another provider's `pyproject.toml` for a change that added a parameter with a `None` default
rationale: Unnecessarily raising the lower-bound breaks users who have the older provider installed; backward compatibility is maintained when new parameters have safe defaults.

evidence.excerpt: google provider will actually work with both old and new cncf.kubernetes provider

rule: Do not add a minimum version constraint to an optional provider extra dependency solely because of a new additive (non-breaking) feature in that dependency.
trigger: diff adds `>=x.y.z` version floor to an optional extra in `pyproject.toml` for a feature addition rather than a breaking API change
rationale: Version constraints on optional extras should reflect genuine incompatibilities; additive features do not break existing integrations.

evidence.excerpt: should probably not add this version constraint, since the new feature is an addition

rule: Use `run_after` (not `logical_date` or `date`) as the parameter name when passing scheduling-time context through hook or utility methods.
trigger: diff renames or introduces a parameter called `logical_date` or `date` in a hook/utility method that carries the DAG run scheduling timestamp
rationale: Airflow is aligning its scheduling vocabulary around `run_after`; using `date` is an intermediate misnaming that will require another rename.

evidence.excerpt: if we want to replace it with `run_after` in the future, let's make it `run_after`

rule: Use camelCase REST API field names (e.g. `"definitionBody"`, `"routineType"`) — not Python SDK attribute names (e.g. `"body"`, `"type_"`) — in the `fields` argument passed to Google SDK update methods such as `client.update_routine()`.
trigger: diff defines a `_WRITABLE_PROPERTIES` list or similar constant using Python attribute names (`"body"`, `"type_"`) passed as the `fields` arg to a Google client update method
rationale: Google client update methods forward `fields` directly into the REST update mask, which expects camelCase names; using Python attribute names silently drops the update mask and causes full resource replacements.

evidence.excerpt: passing Python attribute names may result in update mask being silently ignored

rule: Do not import private modules of a transitive dependency in a provider; if such an import is required, add tracking, tests, and guards against upstream breakage.
trigger: diff adds an import of a symbol whose module path contains a leading underscore (e.g. `from google.genai._api_client import ...`) from a package that is only a transitive dependency
rationale: Private attributes of transitive dependencies break silently after upgrades; the breakage may go undetected without explicit version-pinning guards and tests.

evidence.excerpt: needs guardrails, testing, and tracking so it won't break after upgrading

rule: Declare every directly imported package as a direct dependency in the provider's `pyproject.toml`; do not rely on a transitive dependency being present.
trigger: diff imports a top-level package (e.g. `google.genai`) that is not listed under `dependencies` or the relevant extras in the provider's `pyproject.toml`
rationale: Transitive dependencies are not guaranteed; the installed version may not match what the provider was developed against, and the package may disappear if the direct dependency changes its own deps.

evidence.excerpt: `google.genai` is a transitive dependency — if we import it directly we should declare it

rule: Changing an operator's return value is a breaking change; gate new return-value formats behind a deprecation flag with a `False` default before removing the old behaviour.
trigger: diff changes the return value of an operator's `execute()` (e.g. from a bare filename to a full `gs://` URI) without introducing a backward-compatible flag
rationale: Operator return values are consumed by downstream tasks via XCom; silently changing the format breaks existing DAGs without warning.

evidence.excerpt: changing the returned value could be a breaking change, so we should deprecate it slowly

rule: Inside Airflow triggers, raise `RuntimeError` for unexpected internal states rather than `AirflowException`.
trigger: diff raises `AirflowException` inside a `BaseTrigger.run()` coroutine for an unexpected or internal error condition
rationale: Triggers run in the triggerer process; `AirflowException` is for task-level user-facing errors. `RuntimeError` is the appropriate signal for internal/unexpected trigger failures.

rule: When yielding a `TriggerEvent` with `status: error` under a broad `except Exception` handler, include an operation-describing prefix in the `message` field (e.g. `"Failed while polling <resource>: {err}"`).
trigger: diff yields `TriggerEvent({"status": "error", "message": str(err)})` inside a bare `except Exception` block without contextual prefix
rationale: A bare `str(err)` gives no context about which operation failed; a prefix makes triage significantly faster.

evidence.excerpt: provide more context: `"Failed while polling Agent Engine query job: {err}"`

rule: When adding validation for GCP resource IDs (e.g. project IDs) in a Google hook, include all enforced constraints — both format and length — in the `AirflowException` error message.
trigger: diff adds a regex-based GCP ID validation that raises `AirflowException` but the error message omits the length range enforced by the regex
rationale: Users see only the exception message; omitting the length constraint leaves them unable to diagnose rejections caused solely by ID length.

evidence.excerpt: Update the error message to include the length requirement: 6-30 characters
